title: ​OpenAI Admits GPT-6.2 Billing Miscalculation: Astra Depletes 40% Faster, Sol 25% Faster

content_html:
Feeling like your GPT-6.2 quota suddenly “doesn’t go far enough”? This isn’t an illusion—the problem lies with OpenAI. News on November 27: OpenAI urgently fixed a billing error from the early days of GPT-6.2’s launch. Previously, when most users used GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, plan quotas were calculated at a discounted rate, effectively giving them a quiet discount.

Quota depletes faster, but it’s still a more efficient generation

Thibault Sottiaux, who leads OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT, said that after the fix, completing the same amount of work consumes more quota: compared with last week, Astra users hit their limits 40% faster, and Sol 25% faster. He also reassured users that compared with the previous generation, these two models still use quota more efficiently. The error did not affect other models, and OpenAI will not retroactively recover the undercounted difference.

Compensation: one quota reset, plus free Fast Mode

As compensation, users on the Go, Plus, Pro, and Business plans each get one quota reset. The reset quota can be saved and does not have to be used immediately. Business users have another arrangement: free access to Fast Mode until December 31.

Sottiaux also confirmed that OpenAI has tested a merged Chat and Work mode experience with a small group of Pro users, in preparation for a broader rollout. The merge aims to reduce switching between ordinary conversation and agentic work mode—Work mode can handle multi-step tasks such as executing actions and processing files, but execution is more complex and may also consume more resources.
